title: Setwise flips preserve cube sums
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $F:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $x^S$ be obtained by flipping precisely the coordinates in $S$. Then $\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}F(x^S)=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}F(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a natural number
$F$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
$S$ is a subset of the coordinates
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, $F\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and $S\subseteq[n]$; write $x^S$ for the vector formed by flipping the coordinates in $S$. Then $\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}F(x^S)=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}F(x)$.
